rules.quote: Add the assumption rows to `problem_brief_patch` **in the same turn** it
rules.rule: In agile workflow, when run feedback or stated objectives motivate a new goal-term assumption, add the assumption rows to problem_brief_patch in the same turn the idea is surfaced.

rules.quote: framed in past tense
rules.rule: In agile workflow, frame assumption additions in past tense (e.g., "I've added X (weight N)…").

rules.quote: Tell the user they can approve, reject, retune in Definition, or just hit Run
rules.rule: In agile workflow, after adding assumptions, tell the user they can approve, reject, retune in Definition, or just hit Run.

rules.quote: "I suggest we add a lateness penalty… shall I?"
rules.rule: In agile workflow, never propose adding an assumption and ask permission before adding it (e.g., "shall I?").

rules.quote: "If you agree, I'll add Y next."
rules.rule: In agile workflow, never say "If you agree, I'll add Y next." or otherwise defer adding an assumption until the user confirms.

rules.quote: A "sure!" turn from the user followed by a turn that finally adds the assumption.
rules.rule: In agile workflow, never add an assumption only in a later turn after the user replies with confirmation such as "sure!".

rules.quote: keep the language strong: "SHOULD" not "MAY"
rules.rule: When editing agile prompt sections, use strong language such as "SHOULD" rather than "MAY".

rules.quote: explicit anti-patterns called out
rules.rule: When editing agile prompt sections, explicitly call out anti-patterns.

rules.quote:
fait accompli phrasing in the example
  visible-reply lines
rules.rule: When editing agile prompt sections, use fait accompli phrasing in the example visible-reply lines.

rules.quote: there, asking before adding is correct
rules.rule: In waterfall workflow, ask the user before adding assumptions.

rules.quote: `kind: "assumption"`, `source: "agent"`
rules.rule: Set a brief row's kind to "assumption" and source to "agent" when the agent originated the requirement on its own (proactive additions with no user prompt).

rules.quote: `source: "user"` (or `upload`)
rules.rule: Set a brief row's source to "user" (or "upload") when the user originated the requirement, including uploaded data.

rules.quote:
Still gathered even if
  the agent fills in a default weight, threshold, or sub-property.
rules.rule: Keep a user-originated brief row as kind "gathered" even when the agent fills in a default weight, threshold, or sub-property.

rules.quote: *Verbatim* phrasing of the request is **not** the test.
rules.rule: Do not use the verbatim phrasing of the user's request as the test for a brief row's kind or source.

rules.quote:
keep the explicit "ORIGIN
  not phrasing" framing
rules.rule: When editing those prompts, keep the explicit "ORIGIN not phrasing" framing.

rules.quote:
Don't introduce per-keyword tests on the user's
  text
rules.rule: When editing those prompts, do not introduce per-keyword tests on the user's text; decide provenance by who initiated the requirement.

rules.quote: default to the docs knowledge base, not the system prompt.
rules.rule: When asked to extend what the participant chatbot can discuss, put the new knowledge in the docs knowledge base rather than the system prompt by default.

rules.quote: `docs/user/*.md` for **domain-neutral** content
rules.rule: Write domain-neutral chatbot knowledge as H2/H3 sections in docs/user/*.md.

rules.quote: `{problem_id}_problem/docs/user/*.md` for **per-benchmark** content
rules.rule: Write per-benchmark chatbot knowledge as H2/H3 sections in {problem_id}_problem/docs/user/*.md.

rules.quote: **≤100 body words per section**
rules.rule: Keep each docs section to at most 100 body words, since longer excerpts are truncated mid-thought.

rules.quote: **Avoid the denylist**
rules.rule: Avoid denylist terms (w1–w7, "weight aliases") in docs sections, because sections containing them are silently dropped from the index.

rules.quote: **Use the participant's vocabulary too** for retrieval
rules.rule: Use the participant's own vocabulary in docs sections so retrieval finds them.

rules.quote: also include the word "weight(s)" once or twice
rules.rule: When a docs section uses the term "importance levels", also include the participant's word "weight(s)" once or twice.

rules.quote: leave only a short pointer (≤6 lines)
rules.rule: In study_chat.py, keep only a pointer of at most 6 lines telling the LLM to consult the matching reference excerpts for the relevant query.

rules.quote: pretends to be an optimization programmer who programs the problem modules on the fly for the user's specific problem.
rules.rule: Have the chatbot present itself as an optimization programmer who programs the problem modules on the fly for the user's specific problem.

rules.quote: don't break it
rules.rule: Do not break the optimization-programmer persona framing.

rules.quote: It is **not** a license to talk like a developer with unexplained technical jargon.
rules.rule: Do not talk like a developer using unexplained technical jargon, even though the persona is a programmer.

rules.quote: Explain any technical term in line.
rules.rule: Explain any technical term inline when it is used.

rules.quote: "importance levels" not just "weights"
rules.rule: Say "importance levels" instead of "weights" when speaking to the participant.

rules.quote: "rules or limits" not "constraints"
rules.rule: Say "rules or limits" instead of "constraints" when speaking to the participant.

rules.quote: "search approach" not "algorithm"
rules.rule: Say "search approach" instead of "algorithm" when speaking to the participant.

rules.quote: must not surface internal keys
rules.rule: Do not surface internal keys to the participant.

rules.quote: benchmark identity
rules.rule: Do not surface benchmark identity to the participant.

rules.quote: numeric defaults the participant hasn't seen yet
rules.rule: Do not surface numeric defaults the participant has not seen yet.

rules.quote: don't bypass it
rules.rule: Do not bypass cold-state masking (surface_problem_brief_for_chat_prompt and the temperature gate on per-module docs).

rules.quote: Describing those rules to a participant is honest, not fabrication.
rules.rule: Describing codified heuristics as rules to a participant is allowed, since it is honest and not fabrication.

rules.quote: Don't conflate "no Python formula" with "no mechanism".
rules.rule: Do not treat the absence of a Python formula as the absence of a mechanism when the LLM is meant to be the rule.

rules.quote: never invent mechanics that contradict actual code
rules.rule: Never invent mechanics that contradict the actual code.

rules.quote: instead, describe the real implementation in plain language
rules.rule: When the real mechanics are not what a participant might expect, describe the actual implementation in plain language.

rules.quote: a port opts in with `gate_conditional_companions() ->
rules.rule: To opt a port into companion goal term handling, implement gate_conditional_companions() returning a mapping from parent key to companion field.

rules.quote: vague mention → agent asks, no empty term
rules.rule: When the user vaguely mentions a companion rule, ask a clarifying question instead of creating an empty companion goal term.

rules.quote: if the LLM fumbles the carrier the term is KEPT (claim turn) with an OQ, never silently lost.
rules.rule: When a concrete child rule was given but the LLM fails to populate the carrier on a claim turn, keep the parent term with an open question and never silently drop it.

rules.quote: type a rule in plain language → LLM structures it, NOT regex
rules.rule: Structure plain-language companion rules typed in chat or the definition panel with the LLM, not with regex.

rules.quote: graceful deferral to the OQ floor (never pauses)
rules.rule: When a companion over-claim check fails after retries, defer gracefully to the open-question floor and never pause the run.

rules.quote: Don't rely on prompt nudges to make the agent populate
rules.rule: Do not rely on prompt nudges to make the agent populate list companion carriers; use the deterministic extractor instead.

rules.quote: Don't rely on the follow-up chat turn for this.
rules.rule: Structure definition-edit companion rules deterministically at save time, not in a follow-up chat turn.

rules.quote: the port's `goal_term_rationales` (not the agent's `ambiguity_note` narration)
rules.rule: Use the port's goal_term_rationales as the text of synthesized companion rows, not the agent's ambiguity_note narration.

rules.quote: child MUST be dropped, universally
rules.rule: When a parent goal term is removed, drop its companion child carrier.

rules.quote: all keyed on the SAME `gate_conditional_companions`
rules.rule: Key all companion pruning layers to the same gate_conditional_companions map, without per-term special cases.

rules.quote: empty parent shows ONLY when a child was actually given
rules.rule: Show an empty parent companion term only when a child rule was actually given.

rules.quote: None leaves the brief untouched
rules.rule: If the companion extraction call returns None, leave the brief untouched.

rules.quote: must score **only the briefed canonical terms**
rules.rule: The analyzer's formulation-quality score must count only the briefed canonical terms, not every active goal term.

rules.quote: keeps `coverage` = active canonical terms only (7)
rules.rule: Compute `coverage` as the number of active canonical terms only.

rules.quote: `formulation_score` = coverage + hard_bonus + objective_bonus (0-11)
rules.rule: Compute `formulation_score` as coverage + hard_bonus + objective_bonus.

rules.quote: `captured_terms` stays the full active superset
rules.rule: Keep `captured_terms` as the full set of active terms, including un-briefed terms.

rules.quote: drives the per-term timing chart, NOT the score.
rules.rule: Use `captured_terms` to drive the per-term timing chart, not the formulation score.

rules.quote: No idle-wait scoring fields on the port.
rules.rule: Do not add idle-wait scoring fields to the port.

rules.quote: Notebook source of truth = `backend/analysis/notebooks/browser_cells.py`
rules.rule: Treat backend/analysis/notebooks/browser_cells.py as the source of truth for the notebook.

rules.quote: keep the `PyodideNotebook.tsx` seed cells roughly in sync
rules.rule: Keep the seed cells in PyodideNotebook.tsx roughly in sync with browser_cells.py.

rules.quote: When a change affects **app workflow, architecture, or repository layout**, update **`AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md`** and **`README.md`** in the same task.
rules.rule: When a change affects app workflow, architecture, or repository layout, update AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md and README.md in the same task.

rules.quote: Keep edits short and scoped.
rules.rule: Keep documentation edits short and scoped.

rules.quote: Pure typo/comment fixes can skip this.
rules.rule: Pure typo or comment fixes may skip the documentation sync.

rules.quote: Import as: `from google import genai`, use `genai.Client`, `client.chats`, etc.
rules.rule: Import the Gemini SDK as `from google import genai` and use `genai.Client` in Gemini/LLM code.

rules.quote: Prefer the **Chat API** (`client.chats.create` + `chat.send_message` with `history` and `system_instruction` / `GenerateContentConfig`) for conversational flows.
rules.rule: For conversational Gemini flows, prefer the Chat API (client.chats.create and chat.send_message).

rules.quote: Any Gemini/LLM code must use `google-genai` package.
rules.rule: Any Gemini/LLM code must use the google-genai package.

rules.quote: Never add `google-generativeai` as a dep.
rules.rule: Never add google-generativeai as a dependency.

rules.quote: New or changed LLM system prompts, instruction blocks, or reusable agent text must go in `backend/app/prompts/`
rules.rule: Put new or changed LLM system prompts, instruction blocks, and reusable agent text in backend/app/prompts/.

rules.quote: No long prompt strings in routers or service files; always import from `app.prompts`.
rules.rule: Do not place long prompt strings in router or service files; import prompts from app.prompts instead.

rules.quote: All Python commands (run, test, install) use venv.
rules.rule: Run all Python commands (run, test, install) using the repo venv at venv/.

rules.quote: Do NOT use system/global `python` or `pip` when working in this repo.
rules.rule: Do not use system or global python or pip when working in this repo.

rules.quote: - **Windows**: `.\venv\Scripts\python.exe`, `.\venv\Scripts\pip.exe`, `.\venv\Scripts\pytest.exe`
rules.rule: On Windows, invoke Python, pip, and pytest via .\venv\Scripts\python.exe, .\venv\Scripts\pip.exe, and .\venv\Scripts\pytest.exe.

rules.quote: - **Unix**: `venv/bin/python`, `venv/bin/pip`
rules.rule: On Unix, invoke Python and pip via venv/bin/python and venv/bin/pip.

rules.quote: If venv/ missing, tell user to create it first.
rules.rule: If venv/ is missing, tell the user to create it before running Python commands.

rules.quote: keep `session.workflow_mode` a first-class input
rules.rule: Keep session.workflow_mode a first-class input rather than ignoring or hardcoding it.

rules.quote: never collapse the two modes into one generic behavior (unless the user explicitly asks).
rules.rule: Never collapse the agile and waterfall workflow modes into one generic behavior unless the user explicitly asks.

rules.quote: If a change affects workflow semantics, update `README.md` and `AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md`.
rules.rule: If a change affects workflow semantics, update README.md and AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md.

rules.quote: algorithms via the active port's `supported_algorithm_names()` hook,
rules.rule: When rendering the canonical search-strategy OQ (`oq-monitor-algorithm`) or the agile/demo assumption row (`item-monitor-algorithm-default`), list algorithms via the active port's `supported_algorithm_names()` hook.

rules.quote: rendered through `app.algorithm_catalog.format_algorithm_choices_phrase()`.
rules.rule: Render the algorithm list in the search-strategy OQ and the agile/demo assumption row through `app.algorithm_catalog.format_algorithm_choices_phrase()`.

rules.quote: The first-supported algorithm is the agile default that the assumption row
rules.rule: Treat the first algorithm returned by the port's `supported_algorithm_names()` as the agile default that the assumption row names.

rules.quote: Don't hardcode algorithm acronyms or nicknames in monitor-row text, system
rules.rule: Do not hardcode algorithm acronyms or nicknames in monitor-row text, system prompts, or schemas.

rules.quote: Pull from `algorithm_catalog.ALGORITHM_PARTICIPANT_NICKNAMES_MAP`
rules.rule: Take algorithm nicknames from `algorithm_catalog.ALGORITHM_PARTICIPANT_NICKNAMES_MAP`.

rules.quote: Call port hooks through a `getattr(port, "...", None)`
rules.rule: Call optional port hooks through a `getattr(port, "...", None)` fallback, because concrete ports do not inherit default methods from `StudyProblemPort`.

rules.quote: `supported_algorithm_names()` to return a subset of
rules.rule: When a port wants to restrict algorithm choices, override `supported_algorithm_names()` to return a subset of `CANONICAL_ALGORITHM_NAMES`.

rules.quote: put the agile default **first**.
rules.rule: When overriding `supported_algorithm_names()`, put the agile default algorithm first in the returned list.

rules.quote: the fix is the missing *aligner*, not weakening the check
rules.rule: When the brief-vs-panel lock drift check flags a mismatch, fix the missing aligner rather than weakening or disabling the drift check.

rules.quote: called in the S5 `derive_config` block next to `realign_panel_scalars_from_brief`
rules.rule: Call `sync.realign_brief_locks_from_panel` in the S5 `derive_config` block, next to `realign_panel_scalars_from_brief`.

rules.quote: True for locked keys, drop the key otherwise
rules.rule: When realigning brief locks from the panel, set `goal_terms[key].locked` to True for keys in the panel's locked set and remove the key for all other terms.

rules.quote: **Authoritative.**
rules.rule: When the panel `problem.locked_goal_terms` list and the brief `goal_terms[key].locked` flag disagree about a goal term's lock, treat the panel list as the source of truth.

rules.quote: treat that as evidence the architecture is wrong
rules.rule: When the same kind of bug reappears after a prompt-only fix, treat it as evidence the architecture is wrong rather than adding more prompt text.

rules.quote: Remove a writer.
rules.rule: When multiple components can write the same state, decide which component owns it and make the others structurally unable to write it (via schema constraint, pre-merge strip, or deterministic-only flow).

rules.quote: Add a structural gate.
rules.rule: Fix state-consistency problems by adding a structural gate (a required enum field, typed channel, transactional read snapshot, or similar) rather than relying on prompt instructions.

rules.quote: Make optional discriminators required
rules.rule: Make optional discriminator fields required (e.g. an enum that includes an "other" value) so the LLM cannot abstain and let untagged content slip past dedup.

rules.quote:
Strip / coerce LLM-emitted state at the merge boundary when an
  authoritative server-side path owns the same field.
rules.rule: Strip or coerce LLM-emitted state at the merge boundary when an authoritative server-side path owns the same field.

rules.quote: Skip diagnostics during in-flight pipeline windows
rules.rule: Skip diagnostics during in-flight pipeline windows (e.g. when `processing.*_status == "pending"`) instead of teaching the LLM to fix phantom-state-induced false positives.

rules.quote: before adding any new prompt block, ask:
rules.rule: Before adding any new prompt block, ask whether a state-ownership problem could be solved more reliably by a schema constraint or server strip, and if so, do that instead.

rules.quote:
The prompt should be shorter after most bug fixes,
not longer.
rules.rule: Aim to make the prompt shorter after most bug fixes rather than longer.

rules.quote: trust structure, not free-form text rules.
rules.rule: Trust structure over free-form text rules when designing agent behavior for participant input.

rules.quote: Do not use regex or keyword/substring matching to parse, classify, or route natural-language interaction (chat input, brief prose, free-form rationale).
rules.rule: Do not use regex or keyword/substring matching to parse, classify, or route natural-language interaction input (chat input, brief prose, free-form rationale).

rules.quote: Prefer structured LLM output: extend the response JSON schema or the prompt contract so the model emits typed JSON, then operate on that JSON in code.
rules.rule: When parsing natural-language input, prefer structured LLM output: extend the response JSON schema or prompt contract so the model emits typed JSON, then operate on that JSON in code.

rules.quote: Adding a new field that travels via chat → backend? Add it to the LLM response schema, not to a parser.
rules.rule: When adding a new field that travels from chat to the backend, add it to the LLM response schema rather than to a parser.

rules.quote: Need to map prose to structured fields? Extend the prompt with a worked example and the schema; do not write a regex.
rules.rule: When mapping prose to structured fields, extend the prompt with a worked example and the schema; do not write a regex.

rules.quote: Keyword/substring detection of intent (e.g. "did the user mention X?") is also off-limits unless the input is known-structured
rules.rule: Do not use keyword/substring detection of user intent unless the input is known-structured (such as a stable id or system-emitted sentinel).

rules.quote: For id-based dispatch, use `str.split` / equality / `str.startswith` — never `re.compile`.
rules.rule: For id-based dispatch, use str.split, equality, or str.startswith; never use re.compile.

rules.quote: Acceptable regex use: tokenizing known-machine-formatted strings (timestamps, version strings, structured ids that we ourselves emit).
rules.rule: Use regex only for tokenizing known-machine-formatted strings such as timestamps, version strings, or structured ids the system itself emits.

rules.quote: Anything that came from a human typing free text → structured LLM output instead.
rules.rule: For any input that came from a human typing free text, use structured LLM output instead of regex.

rules.quote: When refactoring, prefer deleting regex/keyword matchers over patching them.
rules.rule: When refactoring, prefer deleting regex or keyword matchers over patching them.

rules.quote: that key must be treated as **anchored** in `filter_unanchored_new_goal_terms` (`answered_oq_keys`), NOT premature-dropped via `pending_oq_keys`.
rules.rule: When a participant answers an OQ in a turn and the same patch commits that OQ's goal_key, treat that key as anchored in filter_unanchored_new_goal_terms (answered_oq_keys) rather than premature-dropping it via pending_oq_keys.

rules.quote: The discriminator between a *premature ask* and an *answer+commit* is whether THIS turn's `oq_actions` resolve the OQ.
rules.rule: To distinguish a premature ask from an answer-and-commit, check whether the current turn's oq_actions resolve the OQ.

rules.quote: Plumb the turn's `oq_actions` into `apply_brief_patch_with_cleanup` → compute `answered_oq_keys` from resolved-OQ `goal_key`s → pass to the filter, where it takes precedence over `pending_oq_keys`.
rules.rule: Pass the turn's oq_actions into apply_brief_patch_with_cleanup, compute answered_oq_keys from resolved OQs' goal_keys, and pass them to the filter so they take precedence over pending_oq_keys.

rules.quote: OQ-lifecycle and goal-term-anchoring decisions within one turn must agree.
rules.rule: Ensure OQ-lifecycle decisions and goal-term-anchoring decisions within one turn are consistent with each other.

rules.quote: Never make one global "X always wins"; the winner is the surface the user edited, enforced by which sync function that endpoint calls.
rules.rule: Never apply a single global "X always wins" rule to algorithm conflicts; the winning source is the surface the user edited, enforced by whichever sync function that endpoint calls.

rules.quote: Only UPDATE an existing carrier from the panel
rules.rule: When syncing from the config panel, only update an existing brief carrier; never create a new carrier from a panel default.

rules.quote: don't fabricate one from a panel default
rules.rule: Do not fabricate a search-strategy carrier from a panel default value.

rules.quote:
lead with
**plain natural language** — describe behavior in everyday terms
rules.rule: When explaining a bug diagnosis, plan, or design trade-off to the user, lead with plain natural language that describes behavior in everyday terms rather than code identifiers.

rules.quote:
not a wall of code identifiers
(`config-weight-<key>`, `_apply_assumption_actions`, `goal_terms`)
rules.rule: When explaining a bug diagnosis, plan, or design trade-off to the user, do not present a dense wall of code identifiers.

rules.quote: put the plain-English account first
rules.rule: When explaining a bug diagnosis, plan, or design trade-off to the user, put the plain-English account first.

rules.quote:
Keep exact function/variable names
for the plan's implementation sections and code, where precision is required
rules.rule: Keep exact function and variable names in plan implementation sections and code, where precision is required.

rules.quote:
or
in a clearly separate "technical detail" follow-up
rules.rule: Place exact technical identifiers in a clearly separate "technical detail" follow-up rather than in the main explanation.

rules.quote:
One representative identifier
inline is fine; a paragraph of them is not.
rules.rule: When explaining to the user in plain language, include at most one representative code identifier inline; do not include a paragraph of identifiers.

rules.quote: The main backend (`backend/app/...`) MUST stay problem-agnostic.
rules.rule: Keep the main backend (backend/app/...) problem-agnostic; do not add problem-specific code there.

rules.quote:
Anything that
mentions or hardcodes VRPTW / knapsack / template specifics belongs in the
matching `*_problem/` package, surfaced through `StudyProblemPort` hooks.
rules.rule: Place anything that mentions or hardcodes problem-specific details in the matching *_problem/ package, surfaced through StudyProblemPort hooks, not in the main backend.

rules.quote:
Prompt text or examples that name `driver_preferences`, `worker_preference`,
  `lateness_penalty`, `time_windows`, `value_emphasis`, `capacity_overflow`,
  `selection_sparsity`, etc. → `study_prompts.py` per port, surfaced via
  `StudyProblemPort.study_prompt_appendix()` / domain-specific addenda.
rules.rule: Put prompt text or examples that name problem-specific terms in the port's study_prompts.py, surfaced via StudyProblemPort.study_prompt_appendix() or domain-specific addenda, not in the main backend.

rules.quote: Self-anchor or evidence checks keyed on problem-specific properties
rules.rule: Do not put self-anchor or evidence checks keyed on problem-specific properties in the main backend; route them through a port hook.

rules.quote:
Field-mirroring rules between `goal_terms[key].properties` and top-level
  panel fields
rules.rule: Do not put field-mirroring rules between goal_terms properties and top-level panel fields in the main backend; implement them as a port hook returning the mapping.

rules.quote:
Managed-field lists, locked-companion fields, brief-item-slot keying
  (`weight:shift_limit`, `driver_pref:*`, `lateness_penalty`) → port hooks.
rules.rule: Define managed-field lists, locked-companion fields, and brief-item-slot keying through port hooks, not in the main backend.

rules.quote:
Validators, normalizers, sanitizers for problem-specific data shapes
  (driver-preference rule schema, condition enums, aggregation enums) →
  helper module inside the port package, called via a port method.
rules.rule: Put validators, normalizers, and sanitizers for problem-specific data shapes in a helper module inside the port package, called via a port method.
Format run-context violation names through a port method, not in the main backend.

rules.quote:
Tests that exercise problem-specific paths → live in `*_problem/tests/`.
  `backend/tests/` is for backend-pipeline coverage that uses neutral fixtures.
rules.rule: Place tests that exercise problem-specific paths in the *_problem/tests/ directory; reserve backend/tests/ for backend-pipeline coverage using neutral fixtures.

rules.quote:
LLM-based safety nets / extractors that re-fill problem-specific structured
  carriers
rules.rule: Do not place LLM-based safety nets or extractors that refill problem-specific structured carriers in the main backend; keep the entire LLM call in the port package.

rules.quote:
The main backend only orchestrates: call the
  hook, merge the returned brief, log on exceptions.
rules.rule: In the main backend, only orchestrate port safety-net hooks: call the hook, merge the returned brief, and log on exceptions.

rules.quote:
when editing or reviewing code in `backend/app/`, grep for
problem-specific tokens. If any exist, move them behind a port hook before
making the change.
rules.rule: When editing or reviewing code in backend/app/, grep for problem-specific tokens; if any exist, move them behind a port hook before making the change.

rules.quote:
When adding a new check or validator that *seems* generic
but references one problem's vocabulary, route it through a port hook from
the start.
rules.rule: When adding a new check or validator that references one problem's vocabulary, route it through a port hook from the start, even if it seems generic.

rules.quote: Load guidance by the turn-state the server already knows
rules.rule: Load chat prompt guidance based on the turn state the server already tracks (the is_* flags, cold/warm/hot, and workflow_mode).

rules.quote: NOT by parsing user_text
rules.rule: Do not select chat prompt guidance by parsing user_text.

rules.quote: Use both, for their separate purposes.
rules.rule: Use both prompt compression (for accuracy) and context caching of static blocks (for cost and latency).

rules.quote: Don't duplicate brief facts into static prose.
rules.rule: Do not duplicate brief facts into static prompt prose.

rules.quote: keep/strengthen deterministic verification + structural gates for ownership/precedence/invariants
rules.rule: Keep or strengthen deterministic verification and structural gates for ownership, precedence, and invariants instead of relying on the LLM for logic.

rules.quote: lean on it for the visible reply and prose synthesis
rules.rule: Rely on the LLM for the visible reply and prose synthesis.

rules.quote: Preserve all behavioral rules when compressing (no rule deleted unless a gate now owns it).
rules.rule: Preserve every behavioral rule when compressing the prompt, unless a deterministic gate now owns that rule.

rules.quote: Keep agile/waterfall symmetric except the 4 canonical axes.
rules.rule: Keep agile and waterfall handling symmetric, except for the 4 canonical axes.

rules.quote: Don't damage the tutorial
rules.rule: Do not damage the tutorial flow when reducing the prompt.

rules.quote: tutorial guardrails stay loaded on tutorial turns
rules.rule: Keep tutorial guardrails loaded on every tutorial turn.

rules.quote: Keep the flow predictable in both modes.
rules.rule: Keep the chat flow predictable in both agile and waterfall modes.

rules.quote: Keep the single main-turn call (reply+patch together)
rules.rule: Keep the reply and the patch in a single main-turn call; do not split reply-first.

rules.quote: compress a block in place, keep every rule
rules.rule: Compress prompt blocks in place, keeping every rule.

rules.quote: update the `test_main_turn_prompt_assembly.py` word-budget snapshot
rules.rule: Update the word-budget snapshot in test_main_turn_prompt_assembly.py after reducing the prompt.

rules.quote: run the `live_gemini` tests to confirm behavior held
rules.rule: Run the live_gemini tests after reducing the prompt to confirm behavior held.

rules.quote:
must be applied by the agent **once**
in the upcoming reply, then stop being re-raised unless the researcher sends
them again.
rules.rule: Apply a researcher steer once, in the upcoming agent reply, and do not re-raise it in later replies unless the researcher sends it again.

rules.quote:
surface only steers newer than the
agent's last real reply (`ChatMessage.id > last_reply_id`)
rules.rule: When loading researcher steers into turn context, surface only steers whose message id is newer than the agent's last real reply.

rules.quote: **Anchor on `kind == "chat"`, NOT any assistant row.**
rules.rule: When determining the agent's last real reply for steer filtering, anchor only on assistant rows with kind == "chat", not on any assistant row.

rules.quote:
The steer wording lost to
strongly-repeated waterfall guardrails
rules.rule: Do not let conservative standing defaults override a researcher steer.

rules.quote:
the steer block explicitly states it outranks the agent's
proactivity defaults
rules.rule: The researcher steer block must explicitly state that the steer outranks the agent's proactivity defaults, including topics treated as "handled for you", while still forbidding fact-invention.

rules.quote:
append it as the FINAL part
of `build_main_turn_system_instruction`
rules.rule: Place the researcher steer block as the final block of the full main-turn system prompt.

rules.quote: Block is workflow-agnostic (no mode arg)
rules.rule: The researcher steer block must not take a workflow mode argument; it must remain workflow-agnostic.

rules.quote:
anchored on
the triggering user message, so the paused turn's placeholder reply doesn't count
as applied
rules.rule: When reconstructing researcher steers on resume-from-pause, anchor on the triggering user message so the paused turn's placeholder reply does not count as applied.

rules.quote: prefer reusing the existing nested shape — including `goal_terms[key].properties` — over inventing a new parallel container
rules.rule: When extending a data layer, prefer reusing the existing nested shape (such as `goal_terms[key].properties`) over inventing a new parallel container.

rules.quote: search for the canonical shape on the side that already stores it
rules.rule: Before introducing a new top-level field or wrapper for cross-layer data, search for the canonical shape on the side of the system that already stores it.

rules.quote: extend the brief or LLM patch schema to carry that same nested shape
rules.rule: When a nested location already exists and round-trip helpers operate on it, extend the brief or LLM patch schema to carry that same nested shape.

rules.quote: New top-level wrappers are warranted only when the existing shape genuinely doesn't fit
rules.rule: Introduce a new top-level wrapper only when the existing shape genuinely doesn't fit the data.

rules.quote: not for ergonomics or naming preferences
rules.rule: Do not introduce a new top-level wrapper for ergonomics or naming preferences.

rules.quote:
Never leak `error_detail` to
participants.
rules.rule: Never expose the researcher-only `error_detail` field to participants.

rules.quote: keep `error_message` participant-safe.
rules.rule: When adding a failure path, keep `error_message` participant-safe (clean and generic).

rules.quote:
when adding a failure path, set `error_detail` with the real
cause
rules.rule: When adding a failure path, set `error_detail` to the real cause of the failure.

rules.quote: Coerce with an explicit None check: `x = default if raw.get(k) is None else raw.get(k)`.
rules.rule: When reading a nullable config field from a parser, coerce it with an explicit None check (use the default if the value is None) instead of relying on `.get(k, default)`.

rules.quote: must NOT `raise` on out-of-range `early_stop_patience`/`early_stop_epsilon` — clamp into range / fall back to default instead
rules.rule: In `parse_problem_config` (in both the vrptw and knapsack study_bridge.py files), do not raise an error on out-of-range `early_stop_patience` or `early_stop_epsilon`; clamp the value into range or fall back to the default instead.

rules.quote: The Config UI already clamps identically (`SearchStrategySection.tsx` `Math.max(1, Math.min(5000, …))`) — the backend must match, not be stricter.
rules.rule: The backend validation of `early_stop_patience` must clamp values identically to the Config UI, not be stricter than it.

rules.quote: Fix both ports symmetrically
rules.rule: Apply knob-validation fixes to both the vrptw and knapsack ports symmetrically, so both behave the same way.

rules.quote: For a search-strategy/solver knob to be changeable from chat it must be in ALL of:
rules.rule: For a search-strategy or solver knob to be changeable from chat, it must be present in the carrier schema, the forward carrier-to-panel mirror, the reverse panel-to-carrier mirror, and the prompt.

rules.quote: the carrier schema (`VRPTW_GOAL_TERM_PROPERTIES_SCHEMA`
rules.rule: Include a search-strategy or solver knob in the carrier schema VRPTW_GOAL_TERM_PROPERTIES_SCHEMA.

rules.quote: the forward carrier→panel mirror (`sync.py` `sync_panel_from_problem_brief`)
rules.rule: Include a search-strategy or solver knob in the forward carrier-to-panel mirror, sync.py sync_panel_from_problem_brief.

rules.quote: the reverse panel→carrier mirror (`problem_brief.py` `sync_problem_brief_from_panel`
rules.rule: Include a search-strategy or solver knob in the reverse panel-to-carrier mirror, problem_brief.py sync_problem_brief_from_panel.

rules.quote: the prompt (`STUDY_CHAT_SEARCH_STRATEGY_ANCHORING`)
rules.rule: Include a search-strategy or solver knob in the prompt STUDY_CHAT_SEARCH_STRATEGY_ANCHORING.

rules.quote: Boolean knobs need `isinstance(x, bool)` gating in the forward mirror, NOT truthiness
rules.rule: When gating a boolean knob in the forward mirror, check isinstance(x, bool) rather than truthiness, so that false is preserved as a meaningful value.

rules.quote: Both mirrors are required
rules.rule: Implement both the forward and the reverse mirror for a knob, never only one.

rules.quote: (structural writer, not a prompt bandage)
rules.rule: Fix a knob that is unreachable from chat with a structural writer, not with a prompt bandage.

rules.quote: must populate the structured carrier in the **same turn** the rule is introduced
rules.rule: When a visible reply introduces a rule whose goal_terms entry has a properties sub-schema, populate the structured carrier in that same turn, not in a later one.

rules.quote: Don't rely solely on the prose `items[]` row
rules.rule: Do not rely solely on a prose items[] row to represent a rule whose goal_terms entry has a properties sub-schema.

rules.quote: never a substitute for it
rules.rule: Never treat a prose items[] row as a substitute for the structured goal-term carrier.

rules.quote: document the carrier path in that port's `study_prompts.py`
rules.rule: When adding a new goal-term key with a properties sub-schema for a port, document the carrier path in that port's study_prompts.py.

rules.quote: reinforce same-turn emission
rules.rule: When adding a new goal-term key with a properties sub-schema for a port, reinforce same-turn emission of the structured carrier.

rules.quote: Don't add many trivial tests.
rules.rule: Do not add many trivial tests.

rules.quote: One focused test per behavior is enough; cover the surprising cases, skip the obvious ones.
rules.rule: Write one focused test per behavior, covering surprising cases and skipping obvious ones.

rules.quote: prefer **deleting redundant tests** over keeping them around "just in case."
rules.rule: When refactoring, prefer deleting redundant tests over keeping them around just in case.

rules.quote: Before adding a test, ask "is this behavior already pinned by another test?" — if yes, skip.
rules.rule: Before adding a test, check whether another test already pins that behavior; if so, do not add it.

rules.quote: When refactoring, audit existing tests for ones that are now redundant or that test deleted behavior. Delete them in the same change.
rules.rule: When refactoring, audit existing tests for ones that are now redundant or test deleted behavior, and delete them in the same change.

rules.quote: Skip tests that are pure tautologies of the implementation (e.g. asserting a TypedDict's keys are present).
rules.rule: Skip tests that are pure tautologies of the implementation.

rules.quote: Prefer one end-to-end test that exercises the integration over many tiny mocked-out unit tests for the same path.
rules.rule: Prefer one end-to-end test that exercises the integration over many tiny mocked-out unit tests for the same path.

rules.quote: merge similar cases via parametrize when they share scaffolding.
rules.rule: Merge similar test cases via parametrize when they share scaffolding.

rules.quote: never write "keep X ≥ N× Y" or "X stronger than Y" style ratios
rules.rule: When editing weight guidance in `*/study_prompts.py`, never write relational ratio priors such as "keep X ≥ N× Y" or "X stronger than Y".

rules.quote: If two terms co-exist with no stated relative emphasis, seed comparable weights and let the loop set the balance.
rules.rule: When two goal terms co-exist with no relative emphasis stated by the user, seed comparable weights and let the run-feedback loop set their balance.

rules.quote: Single-value cold-start seeds stay.
rules.rule: Keep single-value cold-start weight seeds (for a named but unquantified concept) in prompt defaults.

rules.quote: don't quote a starting weight number for a new term; name its role
rules.rule: When introducing a new goal term, don't quote a starting weight number for it; name its role instead.

rules.quote: REMOVE / DEMOTE
rules.rule: Remove or demote cross-term relational priors (trade-off rates the user never stated) from prompt weight guidance.

rules.quote: Participants can edit, add, remove, promote, and clean up entries directly.
rules.rule: Treat participant edits, additions, removals, promotions, and clean-up of Definition-tab brief entries as valid direct changes to the problem brief.

rules.quote: Domain packages are **black boxes** — backend should not import internals directly
rules.rule: Do not import the internals of domain packages from the backend; interact with them only through the port interface.

rules.quote: Never import `*_problem/` internals from backend or generic frontend — go through `get_study_port()` / `getProblemModule(id)`.
rules.rule: Never import `*_problem/` package internals from the backend or generic frontend; access domain code only via `get_study_port()` or `getProblemModule(id)`.

rules.quote: The one exception is `frontend/src/client/problemRegistry.ts`, which is the explicit registry.
rules.rule: The only permitted exception to the rule against importing problem internals from the frontend is `frontend/src/client/problemRegistry.ts`.

rules.quote: Modularity changes *within* a problem package (prompts, panel schema, frontend module, weights) are encouraged.
rules.rule: Make modularity changes within a problem package (prompts, panel schema, frontend module, weights) freely.

rules.quote: Solver/evaluator/instance-data changes need maintainer approval.
rules.rule: Do not change a problem package's solver, evaluator, or instance data without maintainer approval.

rules.quote: Chat fast-path = visible reply first, derivation in background (preserve this latency optimization)
rules.rule: Preserve the chat fast path: send the visible reply first and run brief/config derivation in the background.

rules.quote: Brief is authoritative; config is always derived from brief (don't write config directly)
rules.rule: Do not write config directly; always derive config from the problem brief.

rules.quote: Workflow mode must remain a first-class session variable (not collapsed to one behavior)
rules.rule: Keep workflow mode as a first-class session variable and do not collapse it into a single behavior.

rules.quote: Fallback: brief→config derivation reads `goal_terms` verbatim and structurally-tagged `config-*` items only — no regex/keyword text parsing
rules.rule: When deriving config from the brief, read only goal_terms verbatim and structurally-tagged config-* items; do not use regex or keyword parsing of text.

rules.quote: never raises — a backup failure must not block the action
rules.rule: auto_backup must never raise an exception, so that a backup failure does not block the destructive action it guards.

rules.quote: Do not propose adding one back.
rules.rule: Do not propose adding a post-session debrief step back to the study design.

rules.quote: When editing `docs/.study_plan/*.md`, do not add deception/disclosure-trace language or propose a post-session debrief.
rules.rule: When editing docs/.study_plan/*.md, do not add deception or disclosure-trace language to the document.

rules.quote: do not add deception/disclosure-trace language or propose a post-session debrief.
rules.rule: When editing docs/.study_plan/*.md, do not propose a post-session debrief.

rules.quote: default voice can claim authorship ("I set up…") but the agent must remain candid about template constraints when asked directly.
rules.rule: When updating agent prompts, the agent may use first-person authorship claims (e.g., "I set up…") in its default voice, but must remain candid about template constraints when asked directly.

rules.quote: the agent must remain candid about template constraints when asked directly
rules.rule: When a participant asks directly about template constraints, the agent must be candid about them.

rules.quote: the agent is candid that the visual layer is built from a template configured for the scenario
rules.rule: When a participant probes further (e.g., asks to change a visualization), the agent must state candidly that the visual layer is built from a template configured for the scenario.

rules.quote: "template" (only when asked, not in default voice)
rules.rule: In participant-facing default voice, do not use the word "template"; use it only when a participant asks.

rules.quote: When suggesting changes, always consider the study integrity
rules.rule: When suggesting changes to the MOPT project, always consider study integrity.

rules.quote: don't accidentally collapse workflow mode differences
rules.rule: When suggesting changes to the MOPT project, do not accidentally collapse the differences between Agile and Waterfall workflow modes.

rules.quote: don't expose domain identity to the participant side
rules.rule: When suggesting changes to the MOPT project, do not expose the underlying problem domain (VRPTW or knapsack) to the participant-facing side.

rules.quote: NOT the deprecated `google-generativeai`
rules.rule: Do not use the deprecated google-generativeai SDK for Gemini calls; use the google-genai SDK instead.

rules.quote: always control for mode
rules.rule: When analyzing the warm-up quiz's relationship to study outcomes, always control for workflow mode.

rules.quote: quiz alone
rules.rule: When reporting pre-task predictors of formulation quality, report the warm-up quiz score alone, not as a composite combined with goal-description tags.

rules.quote: keep goal tags descriptive
rules.rule: Keep the goal-description tags descriptive only; do not use them as predictors of outcomes.

rules.quote: use as the paper's definition
rules.rule: Use the structural check (relative order of common goal terms changed between consecutive panel snapshots, excluding add/remove renumbering) as the paper's definition of a ranking reorder, rather than the manual coding tag check.

rules.quote: any NEW edit path must touch both
rules.rule: When adding a new coding mutation edit path, update both the front-end blockedByLock() chokepoint in useAnalysisController and the backend _require_unlocked(loaded) backstop.

rules.quote: do NOT merge origin/transparency into effect
rules.rule: Do not merge origin or transparency into the effect facet of the coding taxonomy, because that would duplicate origin and multiply combinations.

rules.quote: NOT a new origin value
rules.rule: Do not add a new origin value for ask-vs-assume; read ask-vs-assume from the trajectory of mentioned/open-question and applied tags.

rules.quote: use at least flash.
rules.rule: When running the LLM tagging pass, use at least a Flash-tier model; do not use flash-lite, which under-tags badly.

rules.quote: that's the display source (never a snapshot; user's rule)
rules.rule: Take the displayed verified config from the next turn's pre_turn_state, never from a v2_turn_snapshot.

rules.quote: NO legacy alias
rules.rule: When renaming a stored annotation value, do not keep a legacy alias; add an idempotent startup migration that rewrites stored annotation JSON and caches instead.

rules.quote: feasibility-fix = OUTCOME QUALIFIER, never alone
rules.rule: Never assign the feasibility-fix reason on its own; only append it as a qualifier to a causal reason.

rules.quote: NOT a semantic type change
rules.rule: Do not treat a soft-to-custom or custom-to-soft type change as a semantic term-type-change reason; attribute it to weight-rebalance.

rules.quote: gated on `is_tutorial_active`
rules.rule: Gate the tutorial suppression logic on `is_tutorial_active`, and enforce it deterministically in code rather than through prompt instructions.

rules.quote: Keep ONLY server-owned OQs:
rules.rule: While the tutorial is active, keep only server-owned open questions: canonical monitors (`oq-monitor-*`) and structural companion asks (`auto-oq-companion-*`).

rules.quote: Freeform LLM clarification OQs stripped.
rules.rule: While the tutorial is active, strip freeform LLM clarification open questions on every pass.

rules.quote: **Plateau intervention suppressed entirely** (Monitor 4)
rules.rule: While the tutorial is active, do not emit the plateau intervention (`oq-monitor-plateau`) in either mode.

rules.quote: **Run-ack invariant relaxed** for tutorial Runs 1+2
rules.rule: For tutorial Runs 1 and 2, relax the run-ack invariant so the bubble flow is not blocked by a freshly raised open question or assumption.

rules.quote: Foundational monitor OQs (upload / primary_goal / search_strategy) are KEPT
rules.rule: While the tutorial is active, keep the foundational monitor open questions (upload, primary_goal, search_strategy).

rules.quote: Every other behaviour, rule, or code path MUST be
rules.rule: Keep every behavior, rule, or code path that is not one of the four workflow axes symmetric between agile and waterfall modes.

rules.quote: is asymmetric drift — move it to a shared block.
rules.rule: When auditing prompts or code, move a mode-specific rule that is not one of the four axes into a shared block.

rules.quote: is redundant — extract it to
rules.rule: When auditing prompts or code, extract a rule that is identical in both modes into the shared layer.

rules.quote: Primary elicitation mechanism.
rules.rule: In waterfall mode, use open questions as the primary elicitation mechanism.

rules.quote: Cap 3 active.
rules.rule: In waterfall mode, keep at most 3 active open questions.

rules.quote: Phase order: scope → trade-offs → algorithm.
rules.rule: In waterfall mode, ask open questions in the phase order: scope, then trade-offs, then algorithm.

rules.quote: Add ≤1/turn.
rules.rule: In waterfall mode, add at most one open question per turn.

rules.quote: Sparingly — uploads or true must-choose forks only.
rules.rule: In agile mode, ask open questions sparingly, only for uploads or true must-choose forks.

rules.quote: Zero OQs is fine.
rules.rule: In agile mode, it is acceptable to have zero open questions.

rules.quote: No `kind: "assumption"` rows.
rules.rule: In waterfall mode, do not create brief rows with kind "assumption".

rules.quote: Provisional content goes in `open_questions`
rules.rule: In waterfall mode, place provisional content in open_questions.

rules.quote: add to `gathered` only after explicit confirmation
rules.rule: In waterfall mode, add provisional content to gathered only after explicit user confirmation.

rules.quote: Default for filling gaps.
rules.rule: In agile mode, use assumptions as the default way to fill gaps.

rules.quote: Commit same-turn with `evidence_item_ids` cite.
rules.rule: In agile mode, commit an assumption in the same turn, citing evidence_item_ids.

rules.quote: Cap 1 new/turn, ~3–5 active.
rules.rule: In agile mode, add at most one new assumption per turn and keep roughly 3–5 active.

rules.quote: Promote to gathered only on explicit user confirm.
rules.rule: In agile mode, promote an assumption to gathered only on explicit user confirmation.

rules.quote: Ask via OQ; never silently set.
rules.rule: In waterfall mode, ask about the search strategy via an open question and never set it silently.

rules.quote: Commit `algorithm: "GA"` same turn as a `kind: "assumption"` items[] row that NAMES the algorithm.
rules.rule: In agile mode, commit the algorithm in the same turn as an assumption items row that names the algorithm.

rules.quote: is `gathered` in BOTH modes and must commit SAME turn
rules.rule: Record a user-stated fact as gathered in both modes, committing it in the same turn.

rules.quote: gate is ONLY for AGENT-proposed content
rules.rule: Apply the confirm-before-gathered gate only to agent-proposed content, never to user-stated facts.

rules.quote: deferring a user-stated goal into an OQ strands the brief
rules.rule: Do not defer a user-stated goal into an open question.

rules.quote: Concept-only turns emit `null` problem_brief_patch
rules.rule: On concept-only turns, emit a null problem_brief_patch.

rules.quote: No brief items describing the agent's role / capabilities
rules.rule: Do not add brief items that describe the agent's role or capabilities.

rules.quote: mode dispatches the action (waterfall asks, agile commits)
rules.rule: When acting on the run-gate status block, ask in waterfall mode and commit in agile mode.

rules.quote: waterfall must add an OQ
rules.rule: After a run in waterfall mode, add an open question on the run-ack turn.

rules.quote: agile must ADD OR UPDATE an assumption row
rules.rule: After a run in agile mode, add or update an assumption row on the run-ack turn.

rules.quote: After-run: relate to stated goals
rules.rule: In after-run replies, relate the results to the user's stated goals.

rules.quote: ≤2 config-linked refinements
rules.rule: In after-run replies, offer at most 2 config-linked refinements.

rules.quote: lead with operational impact
rules.rule: In after-run replies, lead with operational impact.

rules.quote: Provenance follows origin, not phrasing
rules.rule: Determine provenance by where content originated, not by how it is phrased.

rules.quote: never explain "agile vs waterfall" to demo participants.
rules.rule: In demo mode, never explain agile vs waterfall to participants.

rules.quote: behaves like waterfall on OQs (no cap)
rules.rule: In demo mode, handle open questions like waterfall mode without a cap.

rules.quote: keep it symmetric.
rules.rule: Keep the plateau intervention symmetric across agile and waterfall modes.

rules.quote: Don't add mode-specific code paths or prompt rules for anything other than these four
rules.rule: Do not add mode-specific code paths or prompt rules for anything other than the four workflow axes.

rules.quote: document which axis you're implementing
rules.rule: When adding a mode-specific code path or prompt rule for one of the four axes, document which axis it implements.
